Definition: from G1289; dispersion, i.e. (specially and concretely) the (converted) Israelite resident in Gentile countries:--(which are) scattered (abroad).
BiblicalUsage: The dispersion is the scattering itself, the Jews living far from Jerusalem among the nations. Peter writes to the strangers scattered through Pontus and Asia, James writes to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, and the Greeks ask where Jesus will go, to the dispersed among the Gentiles.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the dispersion is the church's address. God's people have always lived scattered among the nations, and the letters to them are letters to us — strangers and pilgrims, waiting for home.
